newsitem.title: ITALY: New Ribor future debuts well on Italy MIF market.
newsitem.headline: New Ribor future debuts well on Italy MIF market.

text.p: The Italian futures market MIF's new futures derivative contract based on one-month Ribor (Rome Interbank Offered Rate) had a successful debut on Monday, operators said.

Lots traded for the three expiries, July, August and September, totalled just over 1,000 and prices quoted were for much of the session just a one basis point difference between bid and offer, the minimum movement allowed.

"The traded amounts are in line with the most optimistic forecasts and to have a spread of just one basis point had been a hope," said Marco Malavasi of Banco Bilbao Vizcaya, one of the market makers.

"To develop the market further we still need a 'running-in' period. Six months of work were needed to get the OIS (Overnight interest swap) really going, but the time could be less for the Ribor contract," said Malavasi.

Operators said the new contract's growth would be closely tied to its real use as a treasury covering instrument. "Foreign operators are needed to develop this new product," commented Antonio Carnevale of Deutsche Bank.
"There will be good oppportunities for arbitrage between Ribor and the OIS," another market maker said.
At 1500 GMT, the most-traded July contract was quoted at 93.13 after opening at 93.08, August was at 93.18 against 93.09 and September at 93.25 against 93.17.
